intent: A habit quiz with a body payoff: three kilogram bars that put Italy far down the list, a cups-a-day counter, a split that turns cups into milligrams of caffeine against the safe daily limit, and the coffee break written into the law.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which country drinks the MOST coffee per person?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which country drinks the most coffee per person?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Finland. Finns get through about 12 kilograms of coffee beans a year each.

lines.direction: ease back over the Baltic; three kilogram bars rise on 'Italy' with Finland on top; the Italian flag-ball thinks on 'States'; the cups counter runs 0 → 4 on 'cups' with a cup sticker as Finland pulses
lines.text: Italy manages about 6. The United States, under 5. In Finland that is 4 cups a day.

lines.direction: tighten slightly; the 4 CUPS / 400 MG split lands on 'milligrams'; a warning sticker on 'limit'; a green tick on 'safe' as Finland pulses
lines.text: 4 cups is about 400 milligrams of caffeine, right at the daily limit regulators call safe for adults.

lines.direction: tighten on Helsinki; a snowflake sticker on 'winters'; the Helsinki pin on 'law' and the COFFEE BREAK card; the coffee-break tag and the Finnish flag-ball on 'breaks' as Finland pulses; the pin leaves at the end
lines.text: Why so much? Long dark winters, and a law: 2 coffee breaks a day, written into work agreements.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: 4 cups a day, by agreement. Follow us.
